cells.tense: The bearing is happening right now, and the pen is here with it.
cells.act: feel it alongside them and keep your own side
cells.ask: Spend ten minutes with someone who is in the middle of something hard — no fixing, no advice — while you stay on your own feet.
cells.core:
You can carry a heavy thing and stay soft with it. That is the strength that doesn't need to squeeze to know its own shape. People lean on you because you don't creak under them, and you don't crush them either.

Where something is ending in your life, this is the hour it is asking for. Not the ending you force, and not the one you refuse — the one you let land. Reach for the people who are in it with you. Sit beside one of them in what they are carrying without lifting it off them. That is what your strength is for now.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold what's heavy without gripping it.
cells.verb: bearing what must be borne without breaking or going rigid
cells.place: at a threshold where something is ending so something else can start

cells.tense: A future nobody can write in advance is the one this strength is bracing against.
cells.act: adjust the share until it is fair, then stop
cells.ask: Take one uneven load between you and someone and settle the share — hand part back, claim your part — then leave it alone.
cells.core:
Under pressure you hold on tighter, and the tightness takes over the job the ending was supposed to do. A thing that is over, you're still propping up with your shoulder. What was resilience has turned into a grip, and the grip has taken the whole seat.

What is needed here is fairer than more bearing. Some of what sits on you belongs to somebody else, and setting it down isn't dropping it — it's putting the load back where it came from. Settle one share this week: hand back a piece that isn't yours, or take back the piece that is. Then stop. The floor holds without you propping it, and the people leaning might prefer the room. You could find out.

cells.tense: A door behind you is closed, and you are still standing at it, waiting.
cells.act: put it down and leave your hands empty a while
cells.ask: Set down something you've been gripping past its finish, and go a day with your palms open before you pick up the next thing.
cells.core:
When the weight came, the bearing went quiet. You reach for the quick answer now, and the quick answer is what lands, and the steadier one has stopped being offered. Holding anything feels like it might break you, so you hold nothing, and the nothing has its own heaviness. Going well, this would be a flat, level floor that carries what is set on it and lets it be set down again, with no one the worse for either.

Strength isn't the missing piece. Setting down what you've been gripping past its ending is. Let one thing go on purpose — not by losing it, by releasing it — and walk a day with your hands free. What they hold after will be lighter, and yours.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are already writing in, and you haven't noticed the page.
cells.act: move toward the thing you actually want
cells.ask: Name the thing you'd hate most to lose, and give it an hour — one step, quiet, no plan past that. Wanting it is allowed.
cells.core:
You have been holding things up for a while, and it reads to you as ordinary. What people lean on is not a mood you happen to be in; it is a strength you keep using while telling yourself you're not. The same goes for the times you fell apart. Both get filed by you as passing conditions.

What is actually yours here is a direction. Something drew you before any of this got heavy, and you can still name it if you stop long enough. Pick the thing you'd hate most to lose, and give it an hour this week — one step, no announcement. You knew which one it was before you finished asking. Let that count as knowing.
